skill.description: Guide Go teams through golangci-lint setup, linter selection, warning interpretation, justified suppressions, formatting, and incremental cleanup.
skill.summary: Configure golangci-lint, interpret findings, and improve Go code quality with practical workflows.
skill.author: samber

security_audit.summary: All 55 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown, comments, standard configuration paths, defensive security terminology, or repository metadata. One medium-risk semantic issue remains: the installation guidance fetches an unpinned latest executable.

remediation.issue: The golangci-lint installation command uses an unpinned latest version.
remediation.suggestion: Replace @latest with a reviewed release version and document the expected checksum or trusted package-manager source.

content.value_statement: Go teams often struggle to choose linters, understand warnings, and manage legacy backlogs. This skill provides practical golangci-lint configuration, triage, suppression, and cleanup guidance.
actual_capabilities: Creates golangci-lint v2 configurations with selected linters, formatters, timeouts, and settings.
Explains lint findings and recommends whether to fix or suppress each issue.
Writes specific nolint directives with linter names and justification comments.
Prioritizes linters for correctness, security, style, performance, testing, and modernization.
Plans incremental and parallel cleanup for large legacy Go repositories.
limitations: Does not build GitHub Actions pipelines; it refers that work to a separate continuous integration skill.
Requires Go and golangci-lint to run checks or apply fixes.
Suggested linter sets still need project-specific validation.
Automatic fixes can change source files and still require review.

use_cases.title: Configure a New Project
use_cases.description: Create a balanced golangci-lint v2 configuration with practical defaults and documented exclusions.

use_cases.title: Triage Existing Warnings
use_cases.description: Classify lint findings, fix defects, and add justified suppressions only for verified false positives.

use_cases.title: Adopt Linting Incrementally
use_cases.description: Plan staged cleanup that protects new code while reducing a large legacy warning backlog.

prompt_templates.title: Explain One Warning
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this golangci-lint warning: [warning]. Tell me what it means and whether I should fix or suppress it.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Lint Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a golangci-lint v2 configuration for [project type]. Prioritize correctness and security, set practical thresholds, and explain each choice.

prompt_templates.title: Review Suppressions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the nolint directives in my Go changes. Identify unsafe suppressions and propose specific directives with clear justifications.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Legacy Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an incremental lint adoption plan for [repository details]. Group independent work, protect new code, and define verification steps.

output_examples.input: A bodyclose warning reports an unclosed HTTP response body.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: fix it. Close the response body on every successful request path because the warning identifies a real connection leak.

output_examples.input: A long table-driven test triggers funlen.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: consider a scoped suppression. Name funlen and explain that test length follows the case table.

output_examples.input: A legacy repository has more than two thousand warnings.
output_examples.output: Adopt checks for changed code first, group findings by category, apply reviewed fixes, and reduce the existing backlog in measured stages.

best_practices: Run lint checks after significant changes and before merging.
Fix root causes before adding scoped suppressions with explanations.
Pin the golangci-lint version and review all automatic changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use bare nolint directives without a linter name and reason.
Do not suppress security or resource findings without strong evidence.
Do not apply automatic fixes across a repository without reviewing the diff.

faq.question: Which golangci-lint version does this skill target?
faq.answer: The included configuration targets golangci-lint v2 and uses its version 2 configuration structure.

faq.question: Can this skill run linters?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide or run golangci-lint when the tool is installed and command access is available.

faq.question: Does it create CI workflows?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on linting configuration and local workflows, then refers CI pipeline work to a separate skill.

faq.question: When should I use nolint?
faq.answer: Use it only after confirming an intentional pattern or false positive. Always name the linter and explain the reason.

faq.question: Can it help with legacy repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends checking changed code first and organizing independent warning categories for staged cleanup.

faq.question: Does automatic fixing remove every warning?
faq.answer: No. Automatic fixes address supported findings only. Review every change and resolve remaining warnings manually.
